title: Concept Drift Detection and Adaptive Retraining of Malware Classification Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.13465v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Concept drift refers to changes over time in the statistical properties of data, as compared to the data that was used to train a learning model. Machine learning models for malware detection or classification are particularly susceptible to performance degradation caused by concept drift, as attackers constantly modify existing malware. In this chapter, we analyze two machine learning-based approaches to automated concept drift detection-a novel approach based on One-Class Support Vector Machines (OCSVM) and a previously-studied technique based on Minibatch K-Means (MK-Means). For comparison we also consider Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD), a statistical technique for detecting changes in multidimensional data. We conduct an extensive series of experiments comparing the effectiveness of four learning models, namely, Multilayer Perceptron, Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, and eXtreme Gradient Boosting. translated_title: 恶意软件分类模型的概念漂移检测与自适应再训练
translated_abstract: 概念漂移是指数据统计属性随时间的变化，与用于训练学习模型的数据相比。用于恶意软件检测或分类的机器学习模型特别容易因概念漂移而导致性能退化，因为攻击者不断修改现有恶意软件。在本章中，我们分析了两种基于机器学习的自动概念漂移检测方法——一种基于一类支持向量机（OCSVM）的新方法，以及一种先前研究的基于小批量K均值（MK-Means）的技术。为了比较，我们还考虑了最大均值差异（MMD），一种用于检测多维数据变化的统计技术。我们进行了大量实验，比较了四种学习模型的有效性，即多层感知器、随机森林、支持向量机和极端梯度提升。对于每个模型，我们...
tldr: 本文提出并比较了基于OCSVM和MK-Means的概念漂移检测方法，用于自适应再训练恶意软件分类模型，以应对性能退化问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes and compares OCSVM and MK-Means-based concept drift detection methods for adaptive retraining of malware classification models to address performance degradation.
